solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Had spiced up editorial content

indicators.note: the content of something is what sits inside it, so the letters are found within the words that follow

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the three words

explanation.surface: Someone accuses a newspaper of sensationalising its leader column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had' looks like a verb of possession, but here it means fooled; the answer runs across spiceD UP EDitorial.
explanation.definitionFit: To be had is informal for being tricked or conned, which is exactly what being fooled means.

clue.text: Men on board provide crew scaling craft

parts.note: draughts (checkers) are the pieces played on a board
to man a vessel is to supply its crew
a craft is a vessel

explanation.surface: Sailors are sent on board to crew a boat that is climbing something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men on board' suggests sailors, but the men are the pieces of a board game. 'Craft' does double duty, supplying the vessel and completing the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical drawing is done to scale, so the skill of the draughtsman is a craft of scaled representation.

clue.text: Self-righteous Liberal short of company

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so letters are removed

parts.note: liberal in the sense of generous or plentiful
CO is the standard abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A sanctimonious politician from the Liberal party lacks any companions.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital L makes 'Liberal' look like a party member; it is the adjective meaning plentiful, COPIOUS, which loses CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Pious can carry a disapproving sense of sanctimonious, making a hypocritical show of virtue.

clue.text: 3-D depiction of moon in play

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: a play is a drama
Io is one of Jupiter's moons

explanation.surface: A stage production uses a three-dimensional model of the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: The moon is not ours: Io orbits Jupiter and is a crossword favourite for its two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama is a scenic model with a painted backdrop and foreground figures, giving a three-dimensional scene.

clue.text: Colourful knight leaves full of love after church

indicators.note: coming after means placed later, so one part follows the other

parts.note: CH is the usual abbreviation for church

indicators.note: whatever leaves goes away, so it is taken out

parts.note: romantic means full of love
N is knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A flamboyant knight departs from a church, brimming with love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like foliage, but it is the verb: the knight departs, and N is chess notation for a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Chromatic comes from the Greek for colour and describes things relating to or having hues.

clue.text: Pirate's card game

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to copy someone else's work unlawfully

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pirate' looks like a buccaneer noun but is the verb to copy; the second meaning is the short name for cribbage, a card game scored on a pegboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit one word: copying illicitly, and the everyday short name for cribbage played with cards.

clue.text: Royal attendants in turbulent reign acquiring new skills

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it
turbulent means disordered and churning, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a monarch's train is their retinue of followers

explanation.surface: Courtiers during a stormy reign must learn new abilities to survive.
explanation.walkthrough: A royal train is the body of attendants, not a locomotive; it goes inside a rearrangement of REIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: Retraining is the process of being taught fresh abilities, typically for a different job.

clue.text: Catch badly in marshier ground, conceding one run

indicators.note: ground means crushed up, so the letters are broken and reformed
to concede something is to give it up, so it is removed

parts.note: taken as written
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A fielder drops a catch on boggy turf, giving away a run.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface hides the mechanics: 'ground' is not the pitch but the anagram signal, and 'Catch' means hear.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch words is to hear them, so catching them badly is to hear them wrongly.

clue.text: Gunners waving flag held by sailor in battle

indicators.note: what is held by something is enclosed by it

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor
RA is the Royal Artillery

indicators.note: something waving moves back and forth, so its letters are disturbed

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Artillerymen wave a flag while a seaman fights in a naval battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Gunners are the Royal Artillery, a staple crossword abbreviation, not the Arsenal football club nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Trafalgar is the 1805 naval engagement where Nelson defeated the French and Spanish fleets.

clue.text: Levy for which Brussels possibly gets blame

parts.note: Brussels is an example of a capital city, as 'possibly' flags
to get is to gain
to tax someone with a fault is to accuse or blame them

explanation.surface: A tax is imposed, and the EU in Brussels takes the blame for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brussels-bashing surface points to the EU, but the city is just an example of a capital; tax as blame is an old sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital gains tax is a charge on profit from selling assets, and a levy is a government charge.

clue.text: One'll defend a point after game

indicators.note: coming after means placed later, so one part follows the other

parts.note: taken as written
polo is a game played on horseback
the point of an argument is its gist

explanation.surface: A defender protects a lead of one point after a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defend' and 'point' suggest sport, but the point is the gist of an argument, and it follows POLO.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologist is someone who argues in support of a cause, belief or person under attack.

clue.text: Rogue ultimately splits faction

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is used

parts.note: the final letter
a camp is a group sharing a position, a faction

explanation.surface: A renegade member eventually causes a political party to break apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue ultimately' reads as a phrase, but 'ultimately' belongs to 'splits', and 'splits' is not a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamp is a mischievous person, a mild or playful rascal.

clue.text: Rabbit lover to give back trap

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to give is to sag or bend under pressure
to bag an animal is to catch or trap it

explanation.surface: A pet lover is told to return a snare set for rabbits.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang to rabbit (on) is to chatter endlessly, so a 'rabbit lover' is someone who loves talking, not bunnies.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasbag is a person who talks too much, one who loves to chatter on at length.

clue.text: Get engaged to escort, then split up

parts.note: to take someone somewhere is to escort them
couples who split up part

explanation.surface: A whirlwind romance: engaged to a date, then separated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get engaged' suggests betrothal, but it means become involved in an activity.
explanation.definitionFit: To be engaged in something is to be involved in it, which is what joining in an activity means.

clue.text: Like autocrat on a trip, passed over?

parts.note: someone tripping on drugs is high
to hand something over is to pass it

explanation.surface: A despot on a journey is overlooked for promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip' suggests travel and 'passed over' suggests being ignored; both are read in other senses.
explanation.definitionFit: An autocrat rules without consulting anyone, and high-handed describes overbearing, imperious behaviour.

clue.text: Islander from a small island, one with brown skin?

indicators.note: read as 'wrapped with', one piece goes round the outside of the others

parts.note: a tan is skin browned by the sun
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for small
the Isle of Man
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A suntanned native of a tiny island is described.
explanation.walkthrough: The small island is the Isle of Man, a British Crown dependency in the Irish Sea; the brown skin is the outer layer, wrapping everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tasmanian lives on Tasmania, the island state south of mainland Australia.

clue.text: Odd American dance succeeding twist

definitions.note: screwball in this sense is US slang for eccentric

indicators.note: to succeed is to come next, so one part follows the other

parts.note: to screw is to twist
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A quirky American dance craze follows on from the Twist.
explanation.walkthrough: The Twist is a 1960s dance, which makes 'dance' look like the definition; here twist is just a verb, and the dance comes second.
explanation.definitionFit: Screwball is North American slang for crazy or eccentric, describing a zany person or behaviour.

clue.text: Beer from the East that's fit for a king

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means reading right to left

parts.note: lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: An imported oriental beer worthy of royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From the East' suggests an Asian import, but it tells an across answer to run right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal means royal or kingly, suitable for a monarch in splendour and dignity.

clue.text: Noddy's lack of memory recalled

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters come back the other way

parts.note: no means none, a lack
ROM is read-only memory in computing

explanation.surface: Noddy, the children's toy-town character, is forgetful.
explanation.walkthrough: Noddy is a famous British children's book character, but a noddy is also an old word for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A noddy is an archaic term for a simpleton, and a moron is likewise a stupid person.

clue.text: Sweep up last of slush that briefly forms solvent

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to pan a camera is to sweep it across a scene

indicators.note: only the final letter of slush is used

parts.note: the final letter is H

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter of that goes

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cleaning instruction: clear up the slush that briefly forms.
explanation.definitionFit: Naphtha is a flammable liquid hydrocarbon mixture widely used to dissolve other substances.

clue.text: Voluntary payments or tribute in US a strain, on reflection

parts.note: American spelling of a word for tribute
taken as written

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirrored, so the letters are turned around

parts.note: a strain of music is a tune, an air

explanation.surface: Fees or tributes in America put a strain on reflection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In US' signals the American spelling without the U; the musical strain is a tune, reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: An honorarium is a fee paid for professional services where custom forbids a set price, given as a gesture rather than an obligation.

clue.text: Vexed, if ordered to throttle Labour leader

indicators.note: to throttle is to squeeze someone by the neck, so one piece grips another

parts.note: ranked means placed in order

indicators.note: a leader goes first, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone angrily threatens to strangle the head of the Labour Party if commanded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour leader' suggests the head of the British Labour Party, but it just yields its first letter; 'ordered' means put in sequence, not commanded.
explanation.definitionFit: Rankled means caused lasting resentment or irritation, so something that rankled has annoyed someone.

clue.text: When most events occur, maybe, in Big Brother's terms?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read in two parts: the busiest time for stories
second meaning: the official language of the regime in Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four

explanation.surface: A question about the busiest time for incidents in the language of a surveillance state.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as NEWS PEAK for the first, whimsical meaning; 'maybe' warns that it is a playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: In Orwell's novel the Party invents a pared-down language to limit thought, and Big Brother heads that Party.

clue.text: Colleges in functioning state complete agreement

parts.note: unis is short for universities
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Colleges in a well-run country reach total consensus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In functioning state' looks like a location, but the whole phrase gives a word meaning working.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means acting together in full accord, with everyone saying or doing the same thing.

clue.text: Toboggan losing its rear part drifted off

indicators.note: losing the back end means dropping the final letter

parts.note: a toboggan is a sled
PT is the abbreviation for part

explanation.surface: A sledge loses its back section and slides away downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rear part' reads as one phrase, but 'rear' belongs to the deletion and 'part' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To drift off is to fall asleep gradually, so someone who drifted off went to sleep.

clue.text: Tramp's friend remained with daughter in custody

indicators.note: being in custody means being held, so one piece is enclosed by another

parts.note: lay is the past tense of lie, as in stayed put
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A vagrant's companion stayed behind while his daughter was under arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: The tramp is not a vagrant but the dog in Disney's Lady and the Tramp.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Disney animated film, the pampered spaniel Lady becomes the companion of the stray dog Tramp.

clue.text: Compassion from judge at start of trial

parts.note: a judge hears a case

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A defendant hopes for mercy from the judge as proceedings begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' looks like a noun for the person on the bench, but it is the verb, to try a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart stands for sympathy and kindness, as in having a heart or taking pity.

clue.text: Most tedious diet deals with disorder

indicators.note: something in disorder is jumbled up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The dullest weight-loss plan tackles eating disorders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deals with' looks like a phrasal verb, but 'deals' is fodder and 'with disorder' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadly can mean extremely boring, so the most deadly occasion is the dullest one.

clue.text: College with vacant refectory taking on several partners

parts.note: a poly is a polytechnic, a type of college
and means together with

indicators.note: vacant means emptied, so the middle is removed and only the outer letters stay

parts.note: the outer letters only

explanation.surface: An empty college dining hall hosts a group of business partners.
explanation.walkthrough: Polytechnics were British colleges teaching vocational subjects; most became universities in 1992.
explanation.definitionFit: Polyandry is the practice of a woman having more than one husband at the same time.

clue.text: Retiring Times editor penning books — a turn-off for addicts?

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the letters are read backwards
penning means enclosing, so one piece is held inside the others

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor about to retire is writing books, which some addicts find dull.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper picture misleads: Times is only the multiplication sign. 'penning' encloses the books between the other two pieces, and 'Retiring' then turns the whole lot round.
explanation.definitionFit: A detox programme cuts addicts off from their drug, so it is literally what turns their supply off.
